subject: Operations
title: Walter Shewhart's Control Charts
description: A short lesson to help you apply Walter Shewhart's Control Charts.

hook.text: In 1924, a Bell Labs physicist drew a simple chart. It became the foundation of quality control.

buildup.text: Walter Shewhart tracked factory variation over time, plotting data points against control limits.

discovery.text: His chart revealed which variations were normal and which signaled a real problem to fix.

twist.text: Managers had reacted to every fluctuation. Shewhart showed that most were just random noise.

climax.text: His student W. Edwards Deming carried these ideas to Japan—and changed the world.

punchline.text: One chart taught factories to see signal in noise.

quiz.question: What did Shewhart's control charts help distinguish?
